english.title: Carried out an activity ancillary to an aviation function while impaired by drink / drugs - transport safety
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) carried out an activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTIVITY..), which was ancillary to an aviation function, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FUNCTION..), when your ability to do so was impaired because of

(A)_[drugs]_
(B)_[drink]_
(C)_[drink and drugs]_
(D)_[drink or drugs]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 92(1)(b) and 95 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
performed an activity ancillary to an aviation function
when your ability to do so was impaired
because of drink/drugs

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 94 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003 defines the term "aviation function" and what is an "ancillary activity".

other.powersofarrest: Section 97 provides that a constable may arrest a person without warrant if he reasonably suspects that the person is committing or has committed the offence and is still under the influence of drink or drugs.
other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
